note: context: Yemen, though here referring to the Arabian Peninsula
why: Source reads למכה בארץ אלימן ('Mecca in the land of El-Yemen'); Mecca lies in the Hejaz, not Yemen proper, so Benjamin's 'Yemen' is used loosely for Arabia, as the note says.

book: The Authorised Daily Prayer Book (Singer), supplemented by The Holy Scriptures (JPS 1917) for the Sefard-rite psalms and verses
anchor: the sound of a great rushing: "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place."

why: This is the Kedushah de-Sidra (Uva le-Tzion): the source shows Isaiah 6:3 and Ezekiel 3:12 each followed by its Aramaic Targum (ומקבלין דין מן דין ... / ונטלתני רוחא ...).

book: The New Testament … A Literal Translation from the Syriac Peshito Version
anchor: onium and from Antioch, and they incited the people against them and stoned Paul
note: The Hebrew text writes "Polipos", a variation of Paul
why: Source verse 19 reads לפוליפוס ('le-Polipos') where the passage (Acts 14:19) names Paul, written פולוס in verse 13 of the same page; it is the same person, though more a scribal/typographic corruption than a true variant name.

book: The Zohar (Soncino Press), vol. V
anchor: ut a blessing over him: > **Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord...** And
note: the text attributes this to Isaac elsewhere
why: Zohar III 104a does not assign 'Then you shall delight yourself in the Lord' (Isa 58:14) to Isaac anywhere; it is the first blessing (Abraham's in the standard text), and the verse given to Isaac on this page (Isa 54:17, 'No weapon formed against thee') is reassigned by R. Shimon lower on the same page to David, not Isaac.
